name: Oravel Baobab-Coconut Mist
description: A lightly sparkling still soda — barely carbonated — combining baobab fruit extract with coconut water and a touch of vanilla. Marketed toward Tier 3 wellness culture as a hydration-forward alternative.
flavor_profile: Gentle, slightly citrusy baobab with soft coconut sweetness and a faint vanilla exhale. Almost still, with a silky mouthfeel. Not sweet-forward — more mineral and delicate.
slogan: Quieter than water. Deeper than juice.
cultural_context: Oravel has carved out a corner of the Tier 3 wellness market by appealing to people fatigued by aggressively carbonated, heavily sweetened sodas. It's often served at Tier 3 meditation lounges and biometric wellness clinics. Some users drink it before BCI calibration sessions, claiming it smooths the sync process — Oravel has not confirmed or denied this.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 wellness clinic has been exclusively serving Oravel and reporting unusually high BCI calibration success rates — a neuroscience researcher wants to know if there's something in the formula, or if it's placebo architecture.

Oravel's baobab supply chain runs through a small cooperative in the African growing corridor — the cooperative is being pressured by a corponation to sell exclusive rights, and Oravel is too small to outbid them.

A Tier 4 executive has been secretly funding Oravel to keep it small and exclusive — they don't want their 'discovery' to go mainstream, and they're willing to go to disturbing lengths to prevent a wider distribution deal.
